customer_question: Ahead of our Bluetooth Logo certification testing, we want to confirm our own RF tester (CMW270) correlates correctly with your InterLab RF Test System. Can this be planned using the QUESTIONNAIRES we already submitted for our certification product, and what would we receive from this exercise?
question_variants: Can we validate our own tester against your certification lab's system before doing the real Logo test?
Do you need different setup information for a tester-correlation exercise than for our actual product's certification test?
What do we get back from a tester-correlation test using your reference sample?
Does choosing the correlation-test approach mean we don't need to send you a test sample of our own product?
actual_issue: The customer wanted to validate their own RF tester against the certification lab's InterLab RF Test System ahead of Bluetooth Logo certification testing, using an Allion-owned reference sample rather than their actual product, and it needed to be clarified that this required separate setup information and produced separate deliverables from the customer's actual Logo-certification test.
plain_english_explanation: Before running the real certification test, the customer wanted extra confidence that their own RF test equipment gives the same results as the certification lab's official system. To do that, they don't test their own product yet -- instead, the lab runs (and later lends out) a standard reference sample that both testers can measure, so the readings can be compared directly. This is a separate, smaller exercise from the actual product certification, with its own setup requirements and its own paperwork.
consultant_answer: The customer-provided QUESTIONNAIRES describes the Logo-certification target product and cannot be used to plan this exercise, since the object under test here is instead an Allion-owned reference sample (used to confirm Allion's own RF Test System) that will be lent to the customer. To build the Test Plan and QUESTIONNAIRES for the reference sample, the following information about it is needed: (1) applied voltage, (2) test command type (HCI or 2-Wire), (3) the interface to the RF tester (UART/USB/RS-232), and (4) the model number. The agreed approach was to run the RF PHY test on Allion's own reference sample first (limited to the 1Mbps test), report the results, and then lend that same sample to the customer. The customer subsequently chose to use the Allion reference board for a paid correlation test (quoted at ¥400,000) between Allion's InterLab system and their own CMW270 tester, which meant the customer did not need to separately provide a test sample of their own product for this exercise. The deliverables for the reference-sample exercise are: (1) the test logs, (2) a test report, and (3) a description document covering the InterLab RF Test System's equipment configuration and functionality, compiled as a PDF from the in-house InterLab manual for customer delivery.
decision_logic: A tester-correlation exercise using a lab-owned reference sample is planned and scoped independently of the certification target product's own QUESTIONNAIRES and Test Plan, since the object under test, its setup parameters, and its deliverables (logs, report, system description) are all specific to the reference sample and the correlation purpose, not to the customer's actual product.
final_recommendation: Treat a tester-correlation request as a distinct exercise: collect the reference sample's own setup information (applied voltage, command type, tester interface, model number) to build its Test Plan, run the RF PHY test on the reference sample first and report results, then lend the sample to the customer together with the test logs, report, and an InterLab RF Test System description document; do not require the customer to separately supply a test sample of their own product for this exercise.
risk_if_done_wrong: Attempting to plan the reference-sample correlation exercise using the certification target product's QUESTIONNAIRES would be missing the actual setup parameters needed (voltage, command type, interface, model number) and could delay or misconfigure the Test Plan.
